passage_en: Pure water in an open beaker has reference water potential zero. Dissolved solutes lower water potential; water moves into a cell whose total water potential is lower than that of its surroundings.
review_note: D under ordinary fresh-potato initial-state assumption: atmospheric pure-water reference is zero; initial solute-containing tissue has lower water potential before equilibration/turgor increase. Fully equilibrated tissue could have zero total potential, so preserve fresh unequilibrated tissue assumption explicitly. Questions and evidence all preserve initial, pure water and signs. Original College Board PDF TLS access fails here; OpenStax section 30.5 independently read for zero reference and component formula. Changing source requires supplemental translation binding.
source_locator: Water Potential and Solute Potential; fresh unequilibrated potato assumption

passage_en: Similarity in many corresponding DNA sequences and proteins can provide evidence of close evolutionary relationship. Close common ancestry makes inherited structural similarity more plausible than an explanation based only on similar environmental demands.
review_note: B: Independent molecular correspondence best distinguishes close ancestry from similar ecological function. Sequence similarity is evidence, not logical proof that this particular organ is homologous. NHGRI general Evolution source alone insufficient; Comparative Genomics Fact Sheet independently read for DNA comparisons and evolutionary relationships. en/zh/vi questions preserve many proteins and nearly identical nucleotide sequences; evidence translations preserve probabilistic can/plausible.
source_locator: benefits of comparative genomics; sequence conservation and evolutionary relationships

passage_en: Crossing-over between homologous chromosomes takes place during prophase I of meiosis. It exchanges corresponding DNA segments before homologues separate.
review_note: A: Kimball Meiosis locates pachytene crossing over inside prophase I, not metaphase/anaphase or prophase II. NHGRI glossary gives meiosis but not exact subphase; supplementary original author page resolves this gap. All languages and evidence preserve prophase I and homologous exchange.
source_locator: Meiosis I; Prophase I detailed view, Pachytene

passage_en: Spindle microtubules attach to kinetochores, protein assemblies formed on centromeric chromosomal regions during cell division.
review_note: C: Kinetochore is protein assembly at centromere that attaches spindle, distinct from centriole/chromomere/chromatophore. NHGRI source describes centromeric DNA/proteins but does not name kinetochore; supplementary Kimball Mitosis explicitly names it and attachment. Vietnamese English loan terms retained; Chinese zhuosi dian is accepted attachment-site terminology in this option context. Evidence correctly distinguishes protein assembly from centromeric region.
source_locator: Prometaphase: kinetochore formation and spindle attachment

passage_en: When striated muscle is inactive, tropomyosin blocks myosin interaction with binding sites on actin. Calcium binding to troponin shifts tropomyosin and allows cross-bridge formation.
review_note: B: StatPearls explicitly states tropomyosin blocks actin-myosin interaction and calcium binding troponin shifts it; H zone shortens, myosin head (not tail) binds/hydrolyzes, thick/thin not troponin/tropomyosin themselves. Questions preserve mechanism across all languages. Existing zh evidence says myo-inositol (肌醇) instead of actin (肌动蛋白), a different molecule. Keep question, require corrected supplemental evidence.
source_locator: Cellular Level: Striated Muscle

passage_en: Inositol 1,4,5-trisphosphate is an intracellular messenger that promotes the release of calcium ions from stores inside the endoplasmic reticulum into the cytoplasm.
review_note: B: NLM MeSH IP3 descriptor explicitly releases Ca from ER stores. Original striated-muscle source does not discuss IP3 and must be replaced. Questions preserve IP3 and cytosolic release; Vietnamese second messenger translated secondary substance is nonstandard but retains signaling role in stated release context. Existing evidence ER/SR description needs new binding to actual descriptor source.
source_locator: NLM MeSH descriptor D015544 introductory definition

passage_en: Water-conducting vessel elements undergo programmed cell death during maturation, leaving hollow, reinforced conduits. Functional sieve-tube members instead remain living despite losing their nuclei.
review_note: B: Michaels source establishes dead hollow conducting xylem and living sieve elements, but does not explicitly establish programmed death. Need direct differentiation/programmed-death source before final support approval. All three questions/evidence preserve xylem vessel vs phloem sieve and programmed death; zh more functional is awkward but maturation target clear. Follow-up: full PMC4880555 author review now directly read; expressly states xylem tracheary elements undergo programmed death to become functional. Source support resolved; new source binding needs supplemental translations.
source_locator: Xylem cell differentiation; programmed cell death and fully functional vessels, author scientific review

passage_en: Influenza is an RNA virus that replicates its genetic material and makes viral proteins after entry and uncoating in a host cell. It does not use a DNA intermediate produced by reverse transcriptase.
review_note: C: CDC identifies influenza as RNA virus and replication in respiratory epithelium. Immediately is life-cycle compression (entry, uncoating, nuclear import first), not literal simultaneous instant replication. All three versions preserve alternative viral DNA/reverse-transcriptase claims; evidence properly qualifies after entry/uncoating. Supplementary direct life-cycle source for absence of reverse-transcriptase intermediate still desirable; RNA identity alone is insufficient (retroviruses also RNA), so support pending for exact full English explanation. Follow-up: full author Kimball Influenza page now read; describes fusion, uncoating, RNA copies in nucleus, mRNA translation and budding without DNA step. Source support resolved; use new exact source binding.
source_locator: hemagglutinin fusion/uncoating; RNA copies in nucleus; mRNA translation and budding

passage_en: Colchicine binds tubulin and disrupts microtubules, including the mitotic spindle. Interfering with chromosome segregation after DNA replication can produce cells with additional chromosome sets.
review_note: B: Primary Polemonium colchicine study PMC9570621 explicitly describes tubulin/spindle disruption and reports verified tetraploids; matches mechanism, not guaranteed every cell doubles. Original FDA PDF is a short browser shell here, not verified PDF. Use actual accessible primary experiment as new source binding; existing English/zh/vi evidence mechanism meaning agrees.
source_locator: Introduction spindle/tubulin mechanism; Results verified tetraploid plants

passage_en: A monoclonal antibody preparation traces to a single antibody-producing cell clone and has much less antibody diversity than a polyclonal preparation, which derives from multiple B-cell lineages.
review_note: C: Single B-cell lineage versus multiple B-cell lineages; T cells do not secrete antibodies. en/zh/vi options preserve lineage distinction and evidence same. IUPAC original source remains403; NCI dictionary retrieval is shell without definition. No final source approval based on indexed definition or correct field agreement; keep support pending. Follow-up: full Kimball Monoclonals author page directly read: polyclonal response versus single plasma-cell clone and antibody-secreting B cell. Source support resolved; new source binding needs supplemental translations.
source_locator: introductory polyclonal response; single clone of plasma cells and antibody-secreting B cell; procedure step4

passage_en: Natural selection acts on the combined effects of an organism’s traits. When a single inherited variant has both beneficial and harmful effects, its overall advantage can allow the associated harmful effect to increase with it.
review_note: Retain B: given one gene with beneficial coat pattern and mildly harmful crossed eyes, selection increases a compromise phenotype. Own conditional deduction from stipulated facts; OpenStax19.3 No Perfect Organism supports selection on whole phenotype/net effects. en/zh/vi preserve shared-gene causation, hypothetical environment and tradeoff; no claim independently verified feline mutation.
source_locator: No Perfect Organism; conditional application to stipulated same-gene traits

passage_en: Disruptive selection favors phenotypes near both extremes over intermediate phenotypes. Under that model, a population can contain two common extreme forms with relatively few intermediates.
review_note: Retain D under ordinary classroom descriptive-selection interpretation: two extreme phenotypes common and intermediates rare fits disruptive, rather than directional or stabilizing, pattern. Does not by itself experimentally prove selection or rule out simple genetic polymorphism; evidence states expected pattern when extremes favored. en/zh/vi preserve cream,brown and rare intermediates. Kimball Evolution Disruptive Selection section directly read.
source_locator: Disruptive Selection; classroom pattern interpretation, not proof of causal selection in snails

passage_en: In oxygenic plant photosynthesis, light supplies energy, water supplies electrons, and carbon dioxide supplies carbon that is fixed into carbohydrates.
review_note: Retain B: ordinary oxygenic plant photosynthesis needs light, water electron donor and carbon dioxide carbon source. Other offered sets require glucose input or omit CO2. Not a statement about every bacterial phototroph. en/zh/vi options and formulae preserve same substances. Kimball Calvin-cycle page explicitly describes light transferring electrons from water to NADP and carbon fixation of CO2.
source_locator: opening light/water/NADPH paragraph and Steps that lead to Photosynthesis

passage_en: Vaccination exposes the immune system to an antigen and can expand populations of lymphocytes whose receptors recognize that antigen. This increases the number of responsive cells rather than creating extra kinds of receptors on each cell.
review_note: Retain D provisionally: antigen-specific lymphocytes clonally expand after vaccination, rather than creating new receptor types or antigen-specific macrophages. All published language versions preserve number of lymphocytes versus number/types of receptors. Supporting clonal-expansion source passage still pending; English draft must not be treated approved. Follow-up: full primary Galson et al human hepatitis-B study PMC4703725 read (abstract and relevant results), demonstrating vaccination-associated clonal expansion and antigen-specific plasma/memory cells. Source concern resolved; draft English retained with this new source binding.
source_locator: Galson et al primary human hepatitis-B vaccination study, abstract and results: clonal sequence expansions and vaccine-specific plasma/memory B cells

passage_en: Energy released as electrons pass along the respiratory electron transport chain drives proton pumping across the inner mitochondrial membrane. The resulting proton gradient powers ATP synthesis when protons return through ATP synthase.
review_note: Retain C: electron-transport energy pumps protons and their return through ATP synthase makes ATP. The statement concerns coupled utilization, not direct substrate-level phosphate transfer. Full Kimball Cellular Respiration ETC and Chemiosmosis paragraphs directly read; en/zh/vi preserve direction and all4metabolite choices. No obsolete numerical ATP-yield claims used.
source_locator: The Electron Transport Chain and Chemiosmosis in mitochondria; energy coupling only, no numerical ATP yields

passage_en: Some chloroplast proteins must first be directed through the chloroplast envelope and then to the thylakoid compartment. These sequential targeting stages can use separate signal sequences; a protein remaining in the stroma need not undergo the second stage.
review_note: Retain D under most-likely textbook two-stage chloroplast-envelope then thylakoid targeting interpretation. Not all stromal chloroplast proteins require two signals, so preserve most-likely and subtype caveat. en/zh/vi preserve two different signal peptides and destinations. Need explicit envelope/thylakoid two-signal source before support approval. Follow-up: full Alberts NBK26828 section Two Signal Sequences directly read; two-stage envelope then thylakoid sequences explicitly established. Source concern resolved for most-likely chloroplast subtype.
source_locator: Two Signal Sequences Are Required to Direct Proteins to the Thylakoid Membrane in Chloroplasts; full author textbook read via /sites/books/NBK26828/

passage_en: The ability to disperse over long distances can help a species colonize geographically separated suitable habitats. This can facilitate a broad, potentially worldwide distribution, although successful establishment also requires suitable conditions.
review_note: Retain D: long-distance dispersal enables colonization over large geographic ranges; habitat specialization/limited dispersal work against cosmopolitan distribution. It is enabling, not sufficient regardless habitat. en/zh/vi preserve most likely and long-distance ability. Kimball Fungi reports far-travelled spores and worldwide distribution; own causal application of that background, not universal measured dispersal law.
source_locator: spore dispersal over1450km and worldwide fungal distribution; own enabling-cause application

passage_en: Plants build carbohydrates by fixing carbon dioxide with energy and reducing power obtained using light and water. These carbohydrates provide material for organic structures such as cellulose, so atmospheric carbon dioxide and absorbed water supply the main raw materials for organic dry matter.
review_note: Retain C: photosynthesis combines atmospheric CO2 and root-absorbed water into carbohydrates that supply organic dry mass; not bulk uptake of soil organic molecules/minerals. Dry excludes unbound tissue water, not atoms incorporated from water. en/zh/vi preserve dry organic mass and combined water/CO2 source. Kimball carbon-fixation page directly states carbohydrate and cellulose synthesis from carbon fixation.
source_locator: opening photosynthesis chemistry; PGAL to sugars and cellulose

passage_en: A chloroplast has an outer envelope membrane and an inner envelope membrane surrounding the stroma. Thylakoid membranes lie inside the stroma, so a route outward from a thylakoid lumen meets the thylakoid membrane, inner envelope, and outer envelope in that order.
review_note: Retain A: innermost thylakoid membrane, then inner envelope then outer envelope. Strama is published typo in wrong distractor; zh uses stroma equivalent, not a changed valid membrane. en/zh/vi correct sequence identical. Kimball Chloroplasts explicitly lists3membrane types and enclosing lumen/stroma. Own nesting application.
source_locator: three membrane types and lumen/stroma arrangement; own nesting count

passage_en: Parathyroid hormone helps regulate the amount of calcium in the blood. When blood calcium is low, parathyroid glands release more hormone, helping restore calcium availability.
review_note: Retain D: parathyroid hormone regulates blood calcium. MedlinePlus directly explains PTH control of blood calcium and response to low calcium. en/zh/vi preserve serum calcium and all four hormone names; no treatment guidance or quantified clinical claim.
source_locator: What is a parathyroid hormone test? PTH regulation and low-calcium response

passage_en: Hyperventilation removes carbon dioxide from the blood, reducing its partial pressure. Through the carbon dioxide–bicarbonate buffer equilibrium, this reduces hydrogen-ion concentration and raises blood pH before slower compensatory changes occur.
review_note: Retain B: stipulated hyperventilation increases effective ventilation, removing CO2, so PCO2 falls. CO2/H2CO3/HCO3-/H+ equilibrium shifts toward CO2 replenishment and consumes H+, raising pH. Full StatPearls Respiratory Alkalosis introduction/etiology and buffer equilibrium read. en/zh/vi preserve decrease/increase signs and CO2 versus H+ in all4options. Immediate healthy-person effect, before renal compensation; not clinical treatment guidance.
source_locator: Respiratory Alkalosis, Introduction/Etiology: bicarbonate/CO2 chemical equilibrium and CO2 loss during hyperventilation; full author chapter via /sites/books/NBK482117/
